flows.name: The spaces between.
flows.description: Loading, empty, and failed states communicate different problems and useful actions.

1: Creator media dominates the space between a quiet Home header and a labeled dock.
Keep a single active video. Lock background scroll for sheets; restore post ID, playhead and mute preference.
2: The compact shelf expands into a buying decision, while the creator stays in view.
320ms high-damping transition. Continue source video for peek; selected SKU must carry into checkout.
3: Shop the frame links visible products to a numbered product list.
Render tags only for the current time range. Every tag also has an accessible list alternative.
4: A 25% comment sheet exposes the count, pinned conversation and composer.
Grow to 60% for reading; opening the keyboard promotes to 90% or a full-height accessible state.
5: The 60% comment sheet is the default reading and replying state.
Draft survives closing. Replies preserve list position. Sheet gestures start at the handle, never hijack list scrolling.
6: A 90% sheet supports deep conversation without a separate comments page.
Text scaling grows rows. Trap focus for this modal, make covered controls inert, and restore focus on close.
7: Your daily drop is a single editorial story with contextual products.
Mix image-led modules and horizontal video strips; avoid a uniform shopping grid.
8: The edit groups products around a useful theme and creator point of view.
Under $50 contains only current prices below $50. Preserve item position after opening a product.
9: Creator picks make recommendations feel personal and grounded.
Show relationship explanations only when known. No fabricated popularity or ownership badges.
10: Discover combines search, dimensional object categories and trending creator media.
Nine categories: Electronics, Fashion, Beauty, Home, Kitchen, Wellness, Plants, Accessories, Sports.
11: Fashion uses editorial media and topical subcategories to encourage exploration.
Show trending videos, top products and creators, new drops and deals. Retain selected subcategory on Back.
12: Search brings video, product, creator and collection results into one view.
Preserve query and filters. Distinguish connection failure from zero matches.
13: Product detail provides imagery, price, variants, reviews and creator evidence.
Buying controls remain reachable. Ratings, discounts, shipping and returns require current product data.
14: Seen on Drip shows several creators demonstrating the same product.
Match by canonical product ID. Keep paid relationships disclosed. Return from video to the same product.
15: Sizing and reviews answer the remaining buying questions.
Only show sizes for products with size variants. A tote has colors, not invented sizes.
16: A creator storefront connects identity, original videos and curated collections.
Follow changes immediately with a rollback on failure. Collections come from actual creator records.
17: Following prioritizes people the user deliberately follows.
Use chronological recent posts and opted-in reminders. Provide Discover creators when empty.
18: Personal profile keeps shopping history and preferences easy to reach.
Orders open order status, not a new checkout. Keep recommendations below essential account controls.
19: Saved mixes products, videos and collections with useful smart filters.
Bookmark means Save; heart means Like. Price alerts are separate opt-in preferences.
20: Notifications favor useful changes over engagement noise.
Group repeats. Read/unread has a text or shape cue. Resolve stale alerts against current inventory.
21: The bag shows the exact SKU, variant, quantity and price before purchase.
Quantity changes recalculate totals. Removing an item allows undo; stock changes do not replace variants.
22: Quick checkout keeps the source media visible above the purchasing surface.
Hide and disable underlying navigation. Revalidate prices and inventory. Use native wallet controls only when available.
23: Delivery editing sits one level deeper in the checkout flow.
Use explicit labels, address autofill and country-aware fields. Preserve valid fields and revalidate shipping.
24: It's yours returns the shopper to the same feed post.
Show success only after confirmed order state. Illustrative item $78; full order total $84.24 including $6.24 tax.
25: A comparison post supports a side-by-side decision within one feed slot.
Label both products independently. Buying one must never silently switch to the other.
26: Collection posts use horizontal movement inside the vertical feed.
Lock gesture axis after intent is clear. Keep vertical feed navigation available outside the carousel.
27: A mini-review foregrounds the creator’s verdict and the product behind it.
Only show supported ownership, usage-duration or repurchase statements. Keep commerce disclosure visible.
28: A new drop announcement is a quieter alternative to an ordinary feed post.
Use a real release time and timezone. Reminders require explicit opt-in.
29: Create a drop begins with media and product tagging.
Keep drafts through permission, connection or upload failures. Preview before publishing.
30: Save to a collection offers organization without interrupting discovery.
Immediate bookmark feedback; choosing a collection is optional. Preserve a default saved item on dismiss.
31: Stable skeletons explain loading without rearranging the page.
Respect reduced motion. After failure, replace indefinite shimmer with a specific retry action.
32: An empty Saved view offers a clear first step.
Do not manufacture saved products. Return to discovery and explain how bookmarking works.
33: The feed connection state retains available content and offers retry.
Keep cached media, drafts and feed position. Do not label a network failure as an empty feed.
34: A declined payment keeps item and address context intact.
Offer another payment method. Unknown payment status is different: check status before offering retry.
35: An unavailable variant is a choice to resolve, not an automatic substitution.
Keep available options labeled. Any changed price or variant requires review before purchase.
36: No search matches keeps the query and gives a useful recovery path.
Offer clear filters and suggested spelling. Preserve input. Do not show this for failed requests.
37: A small local heart makes double-tap feel tactile without taking over the video.
Double-tap only likes; never unlikes. One count increment per action. 260ms; no burst with reduced motion.
38: A follow becomes Following immediately; the mini-profile offers more context.
180ms label/check change. Optimistic state rolls back on failure, with a retry message.
39: Product scrub previews a small set of variants while the media remains visible.
Hold 350ms, lock horizontal intent, announce the highlighted color. Explicit taps are the accessible alternative.
40: The living shelf moves social actions into a compact horizontal row and preserves the product focal point.
The second shelf is a 44pt Shop this look target. Count only tagged products: tote, knit and denim. Coffee is set dressing.
41: The chosen shade remains explicit, and all purchase information fits into one contextual sheet.
Ink on coral passes normal-text contrast. Selected color uses check + label. Match SKU imagery to chosen color.
42: A clear total and editable delivery/payment details bring the purchase into the same visual context.
The $84.24 total is illustrative. Production tax is calculated from actual checkout data. Make the background header inert.
